infrastructure.notes: Mangla Port operations agreement reportedly handed to a Chinese operator in 2026, raising Indian strategic concerns (per Organiser, Aug 2026)

geography.notes: Shares a roughly 4,100 km border with India

politics.government: Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government under PM Tarique Rahman, sworn in 17 Feb 2026, after winning Feb 2026 elections
politics.prior_government: Interim government led by Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus (Aug 2024 - Feb 2026), which took power after PM Sheikh Hasina was ousted in a student-led uprising and fled to India on 5 Aug 2024
politics.notes: Jamaat-e-Islami made a significant seat gain in the Feb 2026 election, concentrated in border areas near India's West Bengal and Assam, which some analysts flag as a security-relevant shift

strategic_priorities: Balancing relations between India, China, and Pakistan
Resolving the Sheikh Hasina extradition/return question
Deepened ties with China (elevated to 'Community with a Shared Future', June 2026) and Pakistan
dependencies: India remains a major trading partner and, per Indian reporting, sent emergency diesel shipments (~45,000 tons, April 2026) amid fuel shortages
vulnerabilities: Political volatility following the 2024 uprising and 2026 election transition
Border-area political shifts (Jamaat-e-Islami gains) cited as a security concern by Indian analysts
Balancing competing pressure from India, China, and Pakistan simultaneously
strengths: Large population and growing garment-export economy
Strategic geographic position between India and Southeast Asia
New diplomatic leverage from being courted by India, China, and Pakistan simultaneously
